The layout was created because, at the time, all of the letters were arranged in type-bars in a semicircular pattern. So if two adjacent letters were used too quickly, the type bars would collide and jam. The QWERTY layout was based on research + trial & error to determine which pairings were most common in the English language, and put those pairings on opposite sides of the machine.
